title: Induced head shapes are stochastic, with frequencies tracking evolutionary distance

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Induced head shapes are stochastic, with frequencies tracking evolutionary distance

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Under identical octanol treatment, G. dorotocephala regenerates take one of several discrete head shapes, and the frequencies of the shapes are unequal and correlate roughly with the evolutionary distance (from rRNA phylogeny) between G. dorotocephala and the species each shape resembles, with shapes of closer relatives (S. mediterranea, D. japonica) more frequent than that of the more distant P. felina.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.3. The Head Shape Changes Are Stochastic

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We conclude that not only are phenotypic outcomes from physiological network perturbation stochastic (as the same treatment leads to one of several discrete shapes among individuals), but the frequencies are not equal and correlate roughly with evolutionary distance between the worm species these heads resemble.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M, Durant F, Hammelman J, Bessonov N, Volpert V, Morokuma J, Pinet K, Adams DS, Pietak A, Lobo D, Levin M, “Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms”, International journal of molecular sciences (2015), doi:10.3390/ijms161126065; section “2. Results › 2.3. The Head Shape Changes Are Stochastic”. Scope: Octanol-treated G. dorotocephala regenerates; four planarian species placed on an rRNA-based tree

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-girardia-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.59

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Unequal frequencies are directly testable from reported counts, but the evolutionary correlation rests on very few taxa and a rough rRNA tree. Existing data can assess the sample-level pattern but not robustly resolve the general association.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate treatment outcome frequencies from individual worms and regress them against independently estimated phylogenetic distances with uncertainty. The correlation must persist under alternative species assignments and phylogenies.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Phylogenetic distance and head-shape classification are coarse.

Only four morphology classes are compared.

The complete individual-level data are not clearly deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.8
data existence: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.35
operationalizability: 0.85

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public sequences can re-estimate evolutionary distance among the four planarians, which is half of the comparison. The frequencies come from one treatment series reported in the paper, with small groups and bins defined by resemblance. The association can be re-ranked at that limited scope and is not a strong test of a general frequency–distance law.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Rebuild the 18S or rRNA tree for Girardia, Schmidtea, Dugesia, and Polycelis from public sequences, and rank the paper's reported shape frequencies against patristic distance. A rank correlation in the stated direction would support the frequency claim; a reversed or null ranking would refute the rough association.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Rough correlation and post-hoc shape bins leave the association weakly specified.

Animal-level class counts are in a figure rather than a deposited table.
